clue.text: Guide old lady around hazard on road

indicators.note: around says the old lady's letters go round the road hazard

parts.note: a crone is an old woman
ice is a danger to drivers

explanation.surface: Someone escorts an elderly woman safely past a danger on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guide' could be a verb leading the sentence, but it is the noun being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicerone is a tour guide who explains sights to visitors, a name taken from the orator Cicero.

clue.text: First part of African capital one's withdrawn, notes as well

indicators.note: withdrawn says the one is pulled out of the city name

parts.note: Addis Ababa is the capital of Ethiopia; Addis is its first part
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A traveller notes something about an African city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' takes I from ADDIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To add is to remark further, so a speaker who adds something notes it in addition.

clue.text: O' Mice and Men, initially composed as left-wing

indicators.note: composed says the letters are put together in a new arrangement

parts.note: O, as written
taken as written

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of Men

parts.note: its first letter is M

explanation.surface: A garbled title of Steinbeck's Of Mice and Men, apparently composed as a political piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges OMICE plus M, the first letter of Men.
explanation.definitionFit: Commie is a slang term for a communist, someone on the political left.

clue.text: Stimulate new learner I put in uniform

indicators.note: put in says these letters go inside the word for uniform

parts.note: even means uniform, regular
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A trainer motivates a new trainee by kitting them out in uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' sets N, L and I inside EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To enliven is to make livelier, rousing and animating something.

clue.text: Leading part and another taken from actress — I'd a female title role

indicators.note: taken from says those two letters are removed from actress

parts.note: taken as written
the leading letter of actress, A, and another of its letters, T
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: An actress lands a leading part and then another, a title role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading part and another' names two letters: the leading A and a second one, T.
explanation.definitionFit: Cressida is the heroine named in the title of Shakespeare's Troilus and Cressida.

clue.text: Sorted out blunder without anxiety

indicators.note: sorted means arranged afresh, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Once the blunder was sorted out, there was nothing left to worry about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorted out' reads as a phrase, but only 'Sorted' is the signal; OUT and BLUNDER are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Untroubled means calm and free from worry or care.

clue.text: Soak or wash, in a way

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a soak is a heavy drinker
second meaning: one way to wash something

explanation.walkthrough: 'Soak' looks like a verb but is the noun for a drunkard; sponge has the same slang sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sponge is slang for a heavy drinker and also a verb for cleaning with a soft absorbent pad.

clue.text: Move like snake towards bottom, slow and stop

parts.note: to wind is to twist and turn like a snake
down means towards the bottom

explanation.surface: A snake slithers downward, gradually slowing to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind down is to ease off gradually until finally coming to rest.

clue.text: Quickly put together ladder to place above

parts.note: a ladder in tights is a run
up means in a higher place, above

explanation.surface: Someone hastily assembles a ladder to set it up high.
explanation.walkthrough: A ladder in British usage is a run in stockings or tights.
explanation.definitionFit: To run up a garment or structure is to make it hastily, as with a sewing machine.

clue.text: They replaced little piles of sand in river

definitions.text: They replaced little piles of sand
definitions.meaning: first meaning: golf ..., which superseded heaps of sand for raising the ball
second meaning: the ..., a river in north-east England

explanation.walkthrough: Golfers once teed off from small mounds of damp sand before wooden pegs took over.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf tees are pegs supporting the ball; the Tees is an English river flowing past Middlesbrough.

clue.text: Motivation seen in mother after winter

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
spring is the season that follows winter

explanation.surface: Mother finds new energy once winter has passed.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainspring is the chief driving force behind something, from the main spring of a watch.

clue.text: How to get an anagram, of course

indicators.note: the clue tells the solver outright to rearrange the following word

explanation.surface: Someone asks how to make an anagram, as if it were obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as an aside, but course is the word rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A source is where something is obtained, the place one goes to get it.

clue.text: With solid support, a kid's father makes music

parts.note: a rock is something firm to rely on
a kid is a young goat, whose father is a billy goat

explanation.surface: A child's dad, a pillar of support, plays music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child but is a young goat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rockabilly is a 1950s style blending rock and roll with hillbilly country music.

clue.text: Connoisseurs who consume timeless movies online?

indicators.note: timeless says the letter for time is dropped from the films

parts.note: e-pictures, pictures (films) viewed electronically

explanation.surface: Film buffs stream classic movies on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the usual abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: Epicures are people of refined taste in eating and drinking, discerning consumers of fine food.

clue.text: Delivered letter indicating possession — sign in colour

indicators.note: in says these letters sit inside the colour

parts.note: red is a colour
S, as in the possessive 's
a cue is a signal or sign

explanation.surface: A postal item is delivered, marked as belonging to someone with a coloured sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivered' suggests the post, but here it means saved.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone is to rescue them, as in 'deliver us from evil'.

clue.text: Don't blow up things with charges — they could help one get away

definitions.text: they could help one get away

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: to save money is not to blow it
ions are electrically charged particles

explanation.surface: A warning not to detonate explosive devices that would help an escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SAVE to read EVAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasions are dodges or ruses used to escape questions or obligations.

clue.text: Stereotypical heavy drinkers creating trouble or breaking vessel

indicators.note: breaking says the other letters split the vessel apart

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Drunken seamen cause trouble or damage the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: SS, for steamship, is a standard crossword vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Seamen are traditionally pictured as hard-drinking, as in the song about a drunken sailor.

clue.text: Vexatious order crossing line

indicators.note: crossing says the line passes into the middle of the order

parts.note: a ranking is an order of position

explanation.surface: An irritating command to cross a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Rankling describes something that keeps causing bitterness or annoyance.

clue.text: Use special scissors covering slit up in piece of decorative needlework

indicators.note: covering says the scissor word wraps round the other letters

parts.note: to pink is to cut with pinking shears, giving a zigzag edge

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: a slit is a cut

explanation.surface: A dressmaker uses fancy scissors to cut a slit in embroidery.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinking shears have serrated blades that cut a zigzag edge to stop fabric fraying.
explanation.definitionFit: A pintuck is a very narrow ornamental fold stitched into fabric.

clue.text: Pester with an Asian drink, Japanese port

parts.note: to nag is to pester
an is the indefinite article, A
saki is a variant spelling of sake, Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: Someone keeps on at a friend over an Asian drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Nagasaki is a harbour city in Japan on the island of Kyushu.

clue.text: Desert animal a couple raised in modern times

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the letters are read upward

parts.note: a duo is a pair
AD, anno Domini, the era of modern dating

explanation.surface: A desert creature a couple brought up recently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns DUO to OUD.
explanation.definitionFit: The aoudad, or Barbary sheep, is a wild sheep of North African deserts.

clue.text: Missing female, shed a tear outside, showing passion

indicators.note: outside says the tear goes round what is left of shed

parts.note: a rent is a tear

indicators.note: missing says the female pronoun is lacking from the word shed

parts.note: she is a female pronoun

explanation.surface: Someone sheds a tear over a missing woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' reads as a verb with 'a tear', but it is the word that loses the female pronoun, leaving only its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means fervent and intensely enthusiastic.

clue.text: Post-war leader emerging from battle energised

indicators.note: emerging from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A leader comes out of a battle full of energy after the war.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement Attlee was the UK Prime Minister who led Britain from 1945 after the Second World War.

clue.text: It controls amount of moisture I mixed with mud, that is

indicators.note: mixed says these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stirs water into mud and checks the dampness.
explanation.definitionFit: A humidistat is a device regulating humidity, much as a thermostat governs temperature.

clue.text: One of the two letters one should mind by bad and nasty person

parts.words: One of the two letters one should mind
parts.note: to mind one's Ps and Qs is to be polite; P is one of those two letters
ill means bad

explanation.surface: A lesson on manners beside a rude person.
explanation.definitionFit: Pill is informal slang for an unpleasant or tiresome person.

clue.text: Boxers, for example, swap some neat jabs — just the finalists

indicators.note: finalists here means the final letters of each word, and only those are used

explanation.surface: Boxing finalists trading a few tidy jabs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxers' seems to mean fighters, but they are dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers are a breed of dog, commonly kept as household companions.

clue.text: Literary lion using a non-standard lexicon, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: slang is informal vocabulary outside standard usage

explanation.surface: A celebrated author who writes in colloquial language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literary lion' suggests a famous writer, but it is a lion in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Aslan is the great lion in C. S. Lewis's Narnia stories.

clue.text: Getting over the hill? It's about taking it easy

parts.note: C, circa, means about
resting means relaxing

explanation.surface: Someone past their prime is relaxing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the hill' suggests ageing, but it means literally reaching the top of a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: To crest a hill is to reach its summit and pass over it.
